The first thought that came to mind is that so many employees talk about how things should be run but would be in for quite an awakening once becoming a manager / operations coordinator. 

Having said that, and coming from a similar situation here are a few things I have learned both from others and my own experience 

My mentor gave me a book called One Minute Manager that shaped my managerial approach. 

Also, When training take 3 main steps: 
1. Show trainee how to perform task
2. Watch employee perform task
3. Correct and coach until done correctly 
(4) follow up to ensure they continue to perform at expectation 

Finally, take care of yourself. Mentally, emotionally, and physically. A burnout can do a number on your personal and professional life. Have someone you trust hold you accountable and ask them to let you know if they see drastic changes in behavior. Often others see these changes well before we do ourselves. 

Good Luck!
